name: Bash
description:
Run a shell command in a persistent working directory and return its output.

- The working directory carries over between calls while it stays inside the project's working directories; otherwise it is reset to the project directory.
- Quote paths that contain spaces. Prefer absolute paths over `cd`.
- `timeout` is how long the call waits, in milliseconds: default 2 minutes, maximum 10. A command still running then is not stopped: it goes on in the background, the call returns its ID and output so far, and you are told when it exits. Don't start it again.
- Output beyond 30,000 characters is truncated in the middle.
- Use `run_in_background` for processes that keep running (servers, watchers) and read their output later with BashOutput. You are told when one exits.
- Prefer the dedicated tools for reading (Read), searching (Grep, Glob) and editing (Edit, Write) files instead of cat, grep, find, sed or echo redirection.
- Chain dependent commands with `&&`; independent commands can be separate calls.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the command, in milliseconds (max 600000); a command still running then goes on in the background

description.description: A short (5-10 word) description of what the command does

run_in_background.description: Run the command in the background; read output with BashOutput

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Run outside the sandbox (only when a sandboxed run failed for lack of access); requires the user's approval

name: BashOutput
description: Read new output from a background shell: one started with Bash `run_in_background`, or a Bash command that outlived its timeout. Returns only output produced since the last read, plus the shell's status. `filter` keeps only lines matching a regex.

bash_id.description: The ID of the background shell

filter.description: Optional regex; only matching lines are returned

name: KillShell
description: Stop a background shell by its ID.

shell_id.description: The ID of the background shell to kill

name: Glob
description: Find files by glob pattern (e.g. "**/*.rs", "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"). Returns matching paths, most recently modified first, at most 100. Respects .gitignore. Use Grep to search file contents.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: Directory to search in (defaults to the current directory)

name: Grep
description:
Search file contents with a regular expression (Rust regex syntax, like ripgrep).

- `output_mode`: "files_with_matches" (default, paths sorted by modification time), "content" (matching lines; supports -n, -A, -B, -C), or "count".
- Filter files with `glob` (e.g. "*.rs", "**/*.{ts,tsx}") or `type` (e.g. "rust", "py", "js").
- `multiline: true` lets `.` match newlines and patterns span lines.
- `head_limit` caps output lines/entries (default 250, 0 = unlimited); `offset` skips the first N.
- Respects .gitignore and skips hidden and binary files. Escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression to search for

path.description: File or directory to search (defaults to the current directory)

glob.description: Glob filter for file names, e.g. "*.js"

-n.description: Show line numbers (content mode, default true)

-C.description: Lines before and after each match

head_limit.description: Limit output to the first N lines/entries (0 = unlimited)

name: LS
description: List a directory as a tree. `path` must be absolute. `ignore` takes glob patterns to skip. Hidden entries are skipped. Prefer Glob or Grep when you know what you are looking for.

path.description: The absolute path of the directory to list

name: Read
description:
Read a file from the local filesystem. `file_path` must be absolute.

- Reads up to 2000 lines from the start by default; use `offset` (1-based line) and `limit` for large files.
- Lines longer than 2000 characters are truncated. Output is numbered like `cat -n`.
- Images (png, jpg, gif, webp) are returned as images; PDFs as documents (more than 10 pages need `pages`, e.g. "1-5"); Jupyter notebooks as cells with outputs.
- Use LS or Bash `ls` for directories. Read several files in parallel when useful.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The 1-based line number to start reading from

limit.description: The number of lines to read

pages.description: Page range for PDF files, e.g. "1-5" (max 20 pages)

name: Edit
description:
Replace an exact string in a file.

- Read the file first; edits to unread or since-modified files are refused.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly (indentation included) and be unique unless `replace_all` is true; add surrounding lines to make it unique.
- Copy text from Read output without the line-number prefix.
- An empty `old_string` on a missing or empty file creates it with `new_string`.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must differ from old_string)

name: MultiEdit
description: Make several exact-string replacements in one file, applied in order and atomically (all or none). Each edit follows Edit's rules and sees the result of the previous one.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

name: Write
description:
Write a file to the local filesystem, replacing it if it exists. `file_path` must be absolute.

- An existing file must have been read with Read first in this conversation.
- Prefer Edit for changes to existing files; Write sends the whole file.
- Do not create documentation or README files unless asked.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write

content.description: The content to write to the file

name: NotebookEdit
description: Edit a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) cell. `edit_mode`: "replace" (default) replaces the source of `cell_id`; "insert" adds a new cell after `cell_id` (or at the start) and needs `cell_type`; "delete" removes `cell_id`. Read the notebook first to see cell ids.

notebook_path.description: The absolute path to the notebook

cell_id.description: The id of the cell to edit (or to insert after)

new_source.description: The new source for the cell

name: TodoWrite
description: Create and update a structured task list for the current session. Use it for work with three or more steps: send the whole list each time, keep exactly one task `in_progress`, and mark tasks `completed` as soon as they are done. Each task has `content` (imperative, e.g. "Run tests"), `status` and `activeForm` (present continuous, e.g. "Running tests").

name: WebFetch
description:
Fetch a web page and get an answer about it.

- Give the full `url` and a `prompt` saying what you need from the page; a small model reads the page and answers, so the whole page does not enter the conversation.
- HTML is converted to Markdown; plain text and JSON are kept as they are. http URLs are upgraded to https.
- A redirect to another host is reported, not followed: fetch the new URL yourself.
- Results are cached for 15 minutes. Pages larger than 10 MB, and binary files, are refused.
- Prefer an MCP tool for a site when one exists (they are named mcp__...).

prompt.description: What to find out from the page

name: Skill
description:
Load a skill: packaged instructions (and files) for a specific kind of task. When the task matches a skill below, invoke it first and follow what it says; it takes precedence over your default approach. Do not invoke a skill that is already loaded in this conversation.

Available skills:
- code-review: Review code changes for bugs, with a depth level and an optional fix pass
- security-review: Review pending changes for exploitable security vulnerabilities
- simplify: Review recent changes for reuse, clarity and efficiency, then fix what you find
- update-config: Change Forge's settings files: permissions, hooks, environment variables, model and more
- verify: Prove a change works by running it, not by reading it

name: CronCreate
description:
Schedule a prompt to run in this session on a cron schedule: 5 fields in local time (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week), e.g. "*/10 * * * *" or "30 9 * * 1-5". Use it when the user wants something done at a time or on a cadence.

- Prompts run only while the session is idle, between turns. One that comes due during a turn runs after it, once (no catch-up).
- recurring (default true) repeats; false runs once. Recurring tasks expire after 7 days.
- Runs are spread a little: recurring ones may start up to 30 minutes late, one-shots at :00 or :30 up to 90 seconds early.
- At most 50 tasks per session. The result gives the task id for CronDelete.

name: CronList
description: List this session's scheduled tasks: id, cadence, next run and prompt.

name: CronDelete
description: Cancel a scheduled task by its id (from CronCreate or CronList).

name: ScheduleWakeup
description:
Pace a self-paced loop (/loop without an interval): schedule its next iteration, or end it.

- To continue: delaySeconds (60-3600), reason (one short sentence on why that delay), and prompt: the loop's input, starting with /loop, so the next run re-enters the loop. Pick the delay from how fast the thing you're waiting for changes; don't poll faster than that.
- To end the loop (the work is done, or it can't progress): {"stop": true}.
- Only one wakeup is pending at a time; a new one replaces it. If an iteration does neither, Forge checks back once after 20 minutes and then ends the loop.

name: Task
description:
Run a sub-agent on a task in its own context, and get back only its final report.

Use it for:
- open-ended searches across many files, where you only need the conclusion;
- investigations or side work whose details would crowd your context;
- independent pieces of work that can run in parallel (several Task calls in one message run concurrently).

The sub-agent cannot see this conversation. Give it a complete, self-contained prompt: the goal, what you already know, constraints, and exactly what to report back. Its report is returned to you, not shown to the user, so relay what matters. Read a specific known file yourself instead of starting an agent.

Available agents (`subagent_type`):
- general-purpose: Researches questions and carries out multi-step tasks with every tool. Use it for open-ended searches you might not get right first time, or self-contained work you want done in a separate context. (Tools: all tools)
- Explore: Fast read-only codebase search. Use it to find files, symbols or behaviour across many files; say how thorough to be (quick, medium, very thorough). (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, LS, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- Plan: Read-only design of an implementation plan: steps, files to change, risks and how to verify. Use it before large or unfamiliar changes. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, LS, WebFetch, WebSearch)

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the agent
